full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that on 13.08.1960 the erstwhile Government of East Pakistan allotted to one Mohammad Mohib son of Bhagu Mia of 74 Gour Nitai Saha Street, Dhaka through a registered lease deed 144 sq. yard of land in mouza Barabo, Police Station Tejgaon presently Plot No. U/59 Block-D, Mohammadpur for 99 years on lease at a consideration of TK. 30,000.00 at six annas ground rent, Mohammad Mohib constructed a two storied building on the plot. Mohammad Mohib transferred the holding to his two brothers Mohammad Siddique and Md. Habib at a consideration of TK. 30,000.00 through a registered deed of sale dated 16.04.1964. The brothers had a joint business and out of the business some liabilities accrued in favour of Md. Mobil) and to meet the said liabilities, brothers Md. Siddiquc and Md. Habib transferred back the holding to Mohammad Mohib on 14.07.1967. Since then Mohammad Mohib had been residing in the said two storied building and in the petition it is asserted that the said Mohammad Mohib during the war of liberation was very much present in Bangladesh. On 05.03.19783 Mohammad Mohib by a deed of conveyance annexure-E and an affidavit Annexure-D enclosed therewith transferred the holding with two storied building thereon to one Nur Mohammad Miah, the predecessor of thee present petitioners at a consideration of TK. 40,000.0() and also handed over possession of the building to the purchaser Nur Mohammad Miah. Mohammad Mohib died in Bangladesh and Secretary, Mohammadpur Zame Mosque and its adjacent graveyard granted a certificate of death of Md. Mohib and the certificate is lying in the file No. H233/60 of the Deputy Commissioner of housing because the same was annexed with the application for mutation of the names of the petitioners and Memo No. 3035 (Annexure-F) addressed to the predecessor of the petitioners stating that the Deputy Commissioner of Settlement, Ministry of Housing after scrutiny and detailed enquiry into the matter and after enquiry issued the above Memo mutated the name of Nur Mohammad Miah who died leaving the present petitioner No. 1 his Wife and other petitioners as his heirs. At the time of death of Nur Mohammad Miah some of his heirs were then minor and the petitioners since then have been residing in the Holding at U/59 Nurjahan Road, Block-D in the disputed holding and in paragraph 12 and 22 of the petition, the petitioners have categorically asserted that since long they have been residing in the said building. The petitioners were surprised to know that the said holding has been put in the 'Ka' list, after declaring it as an abandoned property. The said list having been prepared and published on 23.09.1986 in the Bangladesh Gazette (Extraordinary) complying the provision of the Bangladesh Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 So, immediately, after the publication of the list vide Annexure-H dated 24.12.1986 petitioner No. 1 herself and on behalf of the other petitioners wrote to the Secretary, Ministry of Works praying for exclusion of the building from the said list but without any result. Hence the petitioners filed the application before the Court of Settlement.
